summary: First-party Iraqi Ministry of Justice evidence confirms a local Al-Shatrah real-estate registration directorate and an official deed/property-map request service. Direct anonymous inspection of the current Ur JavaScript application exposed routes for service information, application, and authentication but no safe public parcel ID-plus-geometry response. No GeoJSON sample is retained and runtime remains held.
queryOutcomes: Separate English and Arabic discovery queries are recorded in city-4947-al-shatrah.json. English discovery found the Ministry of Justice directorate listing and official Ur workflow. Arabic discovery independently found the same first-party sources plus the Ministry announcement describing electronic real-estate services.

requestOutcomes.outcome: First-party Ministry of Justice contact page lists مديرية تسجيل عقاري الشطرة (Al-Shatrah Real-Estate Registration Directorate) under Dhi Qar registration offices. This is local registry-custodian evidence, not parcel geometry.

Official Ur page describes an electronic request for a property deed and map, supplied by Ministry of Justice real-estate registration directorates. The description says the service is currently available in Baghdad and planned for expansion; it requires login/account and owner identity documents, so no authenticated or personal workflow was pursued.
Ministry announcement describes electronic deed, property-map, property-statement and related services; the named initial directorates are Baghdad offices, not Al-Shatrah.

Official Iraqi legislation explains that cadastral/property maps form part of registration records and are prepared through the real-estate registration authority; this establishes legal map context, not an open data endpoint.

Current application JavaScript was inspected. It exposes routes /customer/customer-service-info/, /apply-service/, and /service-auth/; no WMS/WFS/ArcGIS/GeoJSON parcel endpoint or public anonymous geometry request was exposed in the loaded entry bundle.
Service-information route returned the JavaScript application shell; no anonymous parcel geometry response.
Application route returned the JavaScript application shell; no anonymous parcel geometry response and no login bypass attempted.
Authentication route returned the JavaScript application shell; no credentials, private token, CAPTCHA or authenticated request was used.

coverageAssessment.claimedScope: Iraqi real-estate registration system with a named Al-Shatrah/Dhi Qar directorate.
coverageAssessment.verifiedOpenScope: Local registry-custodian existence and official service procedure only; no citywide or countrywide open parcel geometry coverage verified.

scopeLimits: A Ministry directory listing proves a local registration office, not an open cadastral data feed.
The official deed/map service is owner- and identity-oriented and its published availability is limited to selected Baghdad directorates; no Al-Shatrah anonymous map response was obtained.
HTTP 200 application-shell responses are not evidence of parcel-layer availability.
No owner, address, contact, titleholder, personal, tax/account, or other unsafe fields were requested, logged or retained.
No public schema, native parcel identity semantics, CRS, update currency, citywide extent, or geometry quality could be verified.
No exact-point hit, map miss, timeout, or login wall is treated as evidence of citywide absence.
Packet completion is research evidence only and does not admit a runtime adapter.
serialReviewerQualification: not qualified; independent serial review and adapter qualification still required
uncertainty: Iraq has a first-party local registration custodian in Al-Shatrah, but the current public service is a protected transaction/document workflow rather than an open parcel viewer. A separate current map service could exist outside the inspected pages; it was not evidenced here.
